title: A first request the rules cannot read goes to Home's model, and written people fill the tracks with no runs
request: 36.3: give the kinds of help with no runs yet (analysis, preparation, reporting, business) whole conversations with the model's thinking kept; then the owner: push all changes.
spec: The coverage report of 2026-10-28 counted 0 runs and 0 examples for those tracks. Home must not answer a first request it cannot read with 'say it again' when a model is configured; written people (dev only, English, scripted, silver) play those tracks.
plan: Read the written people's own ways of naming two periods
Give an unread first request to the model with its tools
Never start a model turn inside one
Fall back to the rules' words when the model says nothing
Write the people and their runner

decisions.decision: 'compare A with B' takes B as the baseline, 'from A to B' takes A
decisions.why: it matches how 'compared with' was already read and how the written people meant their periods

decisions.decision: A period without a year is never assumed
decisions.why: a guessed year would compare the wrong months without saying so

decisions.decision: A context flag stops a model turn inside a model turn
decisions.why: the model's own tools reach the same unread path; without the flag a tool call would start another model turn

decisions.decision: A silent or failing model turn falls back to the rules' words
decisions.why: the person must never be left without a reply (the review of 36.3)

change: dclab_rnd/draft/business.py (windows reads 'compare A with B' and 'from A to B'), dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py (_to_model, _MODEL_TURN), dclab_rnd.agent_eval.home.sparse (the written people and their runner), tests/test_home_business.py, tests/test_home_sparse.py.

findings.defect: Two first-request tests failed after the review's fallback was added
findings.scenario: A scripted model turn that writes nothing, on an unread preparation request and on a business question with no periods.
findings.cause: The review made _to_model return None when the model's turn said nothing, so the rules' words follow; the tests' mocked model_turn always said nothing, so they saw the fallback and expected none.
findings.fix: The mocked turn now answers by default; a silent turn is its own case, which expects the rules' words.

outcome: Unread first requests reach the model when one is configured and the rules' words otherwise; the written people's runner is ready (dev only, nothing sent without --yes and a cap). No live run is part of this commit.
lessons: When a review changes what a function returns in an edge case, the tests' mocks must be rechecked: a mock that always takes the edge path hides the main one.
risks: The written people were written by the session that wrote Home's rules: their conversations are training data, silver and apart, never a measurement.
